question_a_dielectric.answer: YES -- it dominates, by more than an order of magnitude
question_a_dielectric.deliverable: p <= 3.55e-2 at the measured tan_delta merely TIES the qp headline; a vacuum-gap / suspended shunt (p ~ 1e-2 -> 19.6 us) is the first design that leaves the qp channel dominant. This mirrors paper 1's d_eff finding: the shunt pad is a designed element, not a trivial fab step, and the brief's 'shunt pad, trivial fab' line does not survive this channel.

question_b_radiation.answer: YES -- it dominates at the stored operating point

question_c_retune.answer: PARTIALLY. The retune buys a ~12x longer radiative T1 AT A HIGHER readout efficiency (eta 0.115 -> 0.20), and it widens the kappa ceiling, but it does not close the channel: a 2D photonic gap suppresses only the in-plane guided continuum, the vertical light cone survives, and the drive electrode's floor is untouched by any f_r.

best_trade_at_eta_0p2.robustness: both conventions land on eta ~ 0.20 with T1_rad ~ 5 us; the retune conclusion does not depend on the chi sign audit, only its location (f_r above vs below f01) does.

verdict.bottom_line: the exported T1 stack (4.75 us at x_qp = 1e-6) is missing its two largest lines. With the analytic bulk-Si participation and the free-space short-dipole estimate the stack collapses to 0.134 us, and the qp channel -- the export's headline unknown -- contributes 2.4% of the total rate. Both new channels come with a concrete, quantified design fix and neither is speculative physics: one uses the paper-1 MEASURED tan_delta, the other the paper-1 MEASURED electrode geometry and the P2-PINNED beta.

_meta.title: EXPLORATION: the two missing T1 channels -- shunt-pad dielectric participation and the collection electrode as an antenna at f01
_meta.status: EXPLORATION -- not part of the M6 contract; qubit.json unchanged; no existing artifact modified

p_participation.meaning: fraction of the qubit's electric energy stored in the lossy dielectric of the shunt pad

tan_delta.anchor: 2e-5 MEASURED (photonics.json:geometry.tan_delta, closed by Q_mat = 52075 ~ 1/tan_delta at 145 GHz, driven)

f_env.meaning: environment enhancement of the short-dipole radiation resistance relative to free space
f_env.values: 1 (free space) | sqrt(eps_homog) = 2.862 (homogenised slab) | (1 + n^3)/2 (dipole at a dielectric half-space, Lukosz asymmetry, upper bound)

kappa_geo, eps_eff.meaning: P2 pickup shape factor and effective permittivity; enter only through beta(d_eff) and are inherited unchanged from qubit/coupling.py

V1_recommended_point_reproduced.source: qubit.two_cavity.fine_scan on its stored default grid

V4_R_rad_textbook.note: textbook short dipole (triangular current) at l = lambda/10 is 1.974 Ohm; the Hertzian uniform-current value is 7.896 Ohm. The 4x is the (1/2)^2 current-distribution factor.

coplanar_pad_on_bulk_Si.basis: conformal-map / image result for a coplanar electrode on a semi-infinite substrate: the field energy splits eps_r : 1 between substrate and vacuum, p = eps_r/(1+eps_r) with eps_r = 11.68 (photonics.json:geometry.eps_core)
coplanar_pad_on_bulk_Si.label: ANALYTIC DESIGN ESTIMATE

membrane_interdigitated.basis: suspended/undercut membrane with an interdigitated pad: most of the field returns through air; p ~ 0.3 is the conventional membrane-transmon figure
membrane_interdigitated.label: DESIGN ESTIMATE (order of magnitude)

vacuum_gap_pad.basis: vacuum-gap (parallel-plate over an air gap) shunt capacitor: only the thin support dielectric participates
vacuum_gap_pad.label: DESIGN ESTIMATE (order of magnitude)

measured_tan_delta.TLS_CAVEAT: the 145 GHz Q_mat closure was measured with the cavity DRIVEN, i.e. in the TLS-saturated (high-power) limit, and at 145 GHz / ~ mK it is a bulk HR-Si number. A qubit shunt pad operates at single-photon power and 40.6 GHz, where unsaturated two-level systems raise the effective loss tangent -- typically by 1-2 orders in amorphous surface oxides. tan_delta = 2e-5 is therefore an OPTIMISTIC LOWER BOUND on the loss, and the whole dielectric column of this study is a best case. The grid down to 1e-7 is included only to show what a hypothetical crystalline/vacuum-gap shunt would have to reach.

dielectric.design_rule_headline: p*tan_delta <= 7.10e-7 makes dielectric loss merely EQUAL to the qp headline at x_qp = 1e-6; p*tan_delta <= 7.10e-9 makes it equal to the qp channel at x_qp = 1e-8, and 7.10e-10 makes it a 10% correction there. At the MEASURED tan_delta = 2e-5 those become p <= 3.55e-2 / 3.55e-4 / 3.55e-5.

reconciliation_with_the_100us_target.note: a p*tan_delta cap of 3.9e-8 corresponds to T1_diel = 100.5 us, i.e. a round 100 us design target, NOT to equality with the qp channel at x_qp = 1e-8 (that cap is 7.10e-9, an order of magnitude tighter). Both are quoted so the criterion behind each number is explicit.

radiation.formula: Gamma_rad = (2 e beta n01/hbar)^2 * 2 hbar omega01 * R_rad, R_rad = 20 pi^2 (d_eff/lambda0)^2 * f_env
radiation.f_env_basis: free space = bare short dipole; homogenised slab = dipole embedded in an index-n medium, where R_rad scales as n (eta_0/n * (n k0)^2); half-space bound = dipole lying on a vacuum/dielectric interface, Lukosz asymmetry P_diel/P_air = n^3, giving (1+n^3)/2 relative to free space. n = sqrt(8.1932) = 2.862 is the drive lattice's volume-average index already stored in qubit.json.

d_eff_cancellation_law.statement: Gamma_rad = 40 pi^2 hbar omega01 f_env g_ang^2 / (E_zpf^2 lambda0^2): at fixed g the electrode length and the voltage division cancel EXACTLY. The only lever left is E_zpf, i.e. the readout mode volume.
d_eff_cancellation_law.consequence: shrinking the electrode does not help unless g is allowed to fall with it; the radiative channel is locked to the readout requirement chi/kappa >= 1.

photonic_protection_at_f01.drive_lattice_verdict: a/lambda = 0.0794 at f01: the drive lattice is deeply subwavelength and homogenises to eps ~ 8.19 (qubit.json two_cavity.geometry.gaps.f_r_in_drive_lattice) -- no gap, no protection at the qubit frequency.

slab_TE0_neff_DESIGN_ESTIMATE.meaning: a 2D photonic gap acts on GUIDED (in-plane) modes only. In the drive lattice the slab is 0.04 lambda thick at f01 and barely guides; in the 3.25x-scaled readout lattice it is 0.129 lambda thick and guides well, so a gap that covered f01 there WOULD suppress the in-plane channel. The vertical light-cone channel is NOT suppressed by any 2D gap. Splitting Gamma_rad between the two needs a slab-LDOS/FDTD run: OUT OF SCOPE, stated, not estimated.

drive_electrode_irreducible_floor.statement: retuning f_r can only address the READOUT electrode. The drive electrode radiates at f01 into the DRIVE lattice, whose gap is [137.5, 177.9] GHz -- a 3.4x scale mismatch that no choice of f_r changes. Its d_eff = 20 um and beta = 0.1727 are fixed by the measured 145 GHz coupling. This is therefore a floor on the whole architecture, not a design variable.
drive_electrode_irreducible_floor.removable_only_by: a conducting enclosure below cutoff (needs < c/2f01 = 3.69 mm transverse dimensions against a 28.6 mm chip), a ground plane, or a smaller-mode-volume 145 GHz cavity that buys the same g with less electrode

mode_volume_requirement.law: Gamma_rad ~ g^2/E_zpf^2 ~ g^2 V_mode / omega_r: at fixed g and f_r the ONLY lever on the readout electrode's radiation is the readout mode volume.
mode_volume_requirement.verdict: a Maxwell-scaled L3 at 44.6 GHz has V = 2.29e9 um^3 = 0.85 (lambda/n)^3. Reaching a 50 us radiative T1 at the stored g needs ~0.02 (lambda/n)^3, i.e. a deeply sub-diffraction lumped/slot resonator, not a scaled photonic-crystal defect. THIS is the concrete readout-plane deliverable this study produces.

radiation.FDTD_CAVEAT: the short-dipole R_rad with a scalar f_env is a factor-~4 band, not a number: the true rate is set by the slab LDOS at f01 at the electrode position, which requires FDTD/Green-function work that is explicitly out of scope here. Everything below is quoted as a band spanning free space to the half-space bound.

baseline_channels.note: thermal_floor and parity_bound carry no T1 rate line in the export (n_th = 3.46e-9 and a 1/(pi eps1) dephasing bound), so the baseline stack is qp + 2 Purcell terms, exactly as the exported budget reads it

chi_convention_audit.status: FLAGGED, NOT ACTED ON (exploration finding, adjacent to P5)
chi_convention_audit.question: cavity.chi_dispersive(g, Delta, alpha) = g^2 alpha/(Delta(Delta+alpha)) is correct only for Delta = f01 - f_r. Every call site in qubit/cavity.py and qubit/two_cavity.py passes Delta = f_r - f01.
chi_convention_audit.decisive_test: the two-pole construction chi = chi_01 - chi_12/2 has poles at f_r = f01 and f_r = f12 = f01 + alpha = 38.964 GHz. The package convention instead places a pole at f_r = f01 - alpha = 42.229 GHz, where NO transmon transition exists, and shows no divergence at 38.964 GHz where the cavity is resonant with |1> -> |2>.

impact_on_the_exported_design.why_it_survived_AT4_AT5: the error is (Delta - |alpha|)/(Delta + |alpha|): 3.1% at the 145 GHz drive detuning (AT-4 passes to 3%), but 2.38x at the 4 GHz readout detuning, and it diverges as Delta -> |alpha|. The AT-4 tolerance is 3% and the AT-5 sample point was never cross-checked against an independent chi.

chi_convention_audit.recommended_owner: the P5 / two-cavity owner, not this exploration

gap_protection_window.condition: GAP_lo * f_r/f_cav <= f01 <= GAP_hi * f_r/f_cav with GAP = [137.5, 177.9] GHz at a = 586.74 um

new_constraint_C6.statement: g <= 0.1|Delta_chi + alpha| AND |Delta_chi + alpha| >= 10 kappa, i.e. the cavity must stay dispersive with respect to the |1>-|2> transition as well as |0>-|1>. The P5 window started at Delta_r = 4 GHz, 2.37 GHz from that line, so it never binds there. Inside the gap-protection window the cavity approaches the 1<->2 line, chi diverges and the dispersive expansion fails; without C6 the scan reports a spurious eta -> 1 optimum a few tens of MHz from the |1>-|2> resonance.
